'''Dennis Barden''' is a mathematician at the [[University of Cambridge]] working in the fields of [[geometry]] and [[topology]].<ref>[https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/people/db127/ Faculty profile], Univ. of Cambridge, retrieved 20 February 2015.</ref> He is known for his classification of the simply connected compact [[5-manifold]]s<ref>{{citation|last=Geiges|first=Hansjörg|title=An Introduction to Contact Topology|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RERR4zMDYRgC&pg=PA367|year=2008|series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics|volume=109|page=367|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9781139467957}}.</ref> and, together with [[Barry Mazur]] and [[John R. Stallings]], for having proved the [[s-cobordism theorem]].<ref>{{citation|title=The Novikov Conjecture: Geometry and Algebra|volume=33|series=Oberwolfach Seminars|first1=Matthias|last1=Kreck|authorlink1=Matthias Kreck| first2=Wolfgang|last2=Lück|authorlink2=Wolfgang Lück|publisher=Springer|year=2005|isbn=9783764373153|page=56|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nBY3n1Q8nUwC&pg=PA56}}.</ref> Barden received his [[Ph.D.]] from Cambridge in 1964 under the supervision of [[C. T. C. Wall]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=24441}}</ref>

== Academic Positions ==
Barden is a Life Fellow of [[Girton College, Cambridge]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.girton.cam.ac.uk/fellows-and-teaching-officers-in-mathematics-and-related-subjects|title=Girton College - Fellows and Teaching Officers in Mathematics and related subjects|website=www.girton.cam.ac.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-04-25}}</ref> and emeritus fellow of [[Pembroke College, Cambridge|Pembroke College]]. In 1991, he became Director of Studies for mathematics at Pembroke College, succeeding [[W. B. R. Lickorish|Raymond Lickorish]]. He held the position until Michaelmas 2003, and in his time saw a great increase in the number of applicants for mathematics, with consistently high performances in [[Tripos]] exams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/alumni-development/publications/pembroke-mathematicians/|title=Pembroke Mathematicians|language=en|access-date=2018-04-25}}</ref> He remains an active [[Tutorial system|supervisor]] at Pembroke and Girton College.
